name: Amcor plc
executive_summary: Amcor plc is a global consumer-packaging leader whose investment case rests on scale, defensive end-market exposure, and a step-change in earnings and cash flow following the April 2025 Berry Global merger. FY2026 GAAP net income rose to US$1.1 billion (from US$511 million in FY2025), with adjusted net income of US$1.9 billion and operating cash flow of US$2.2 billion per the Form 10-K. The quantitative screen rates AMC.AX as a **buy**, but the screening snapshot carries no populated value metrics (zero models passed, zero key metrics), so the hook is qualitative: a large, cash-generative franchise trading at a depressed multiple versus its pre-merger profile, with a dividend yield that has attracted income-focused coverage. The central debate is whether Berry integration synergies and portfolio simplification will outrun elevated leverage (net debt US$12.9 billion), rising interest expense, and ongoing restructuring charges — not whether Amcor remains a packaging compounder.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Amcor offers several characteristics that typically screen well once data is fully populated: global #1 scale in flexible and rigid packaging, exposure to nutrition/health/beauty end markets that are less cyclical than industrial materials, and a management framework that prioritises investment-grade credit, dividends, and free-cash-flow redeployment. The Berry merger (completed 30 April 2025; Berry shareholders received 7.25 Amcor shares per Berry share) roughly doubled the revenue base and is driving cost synergies, portfolio rationalisation (non-core divestitures in FY2026 generated US$31 million pre-tax net gain), and operating leverage — adjusted EBIT reached US$2.8 billion in FY2026 versus US$1.7 billion in FY2025 per the 10-K reconciliation.

Cash conversion supports the income angle: operating cash flow of US$2.15 billion (FY2026) and free cash flow of US$1.23 billion (Yahoo fallback; OCF from 10-K). The company declared a quarterly dividend of US$0.65 per share (ASX CDI notice, 12 August 2026), lifted post the January 2026 one-for-five reverse stock split, signalling confidence in post-merger cash generation. GAAP earnings were depressed in FY2025 by merger-related inventory step-up, transaction costs, and restructuring; FY2026 shows normalisation, with reported net income more than doubling.

The quantitative **buy** signal cannot yet be tied to specific passed models — `screening_snapshot.json` shows `models_passed: 0`, `metrics_present: 0`, and `data_quality_score: 0.0`. The thesis therefore rests on business quality and filing-backed financial inflection rather than screen-level metric confirmation. Relative to typical value criteria, Amcor scores on scale, FCF yield potential, and dividend; it scores poorly on balance-sheet simplicity (goodwill-heavy, negative tangible book) and earnings volatility through the merger year.
financial_review:
**Annual results (Form 10-K, FY ended 30 June 2026 — primary source)**

| Metric | FY2026 | FY2025 | FY2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net income attributable to Amcor (US$m) | 1,106 | 511 | 730 |
| Adjusted net income (US$m) | 1,863 | 1,136 | 1,015 |
| EBIT (US$m) | 1,897 | 1,000 | 1,213 |
| Adjusted EBIT (US$m) | 2,813 | 1,723 | 1,560 |
| Interest expense (US$m) | 676 | 396 | 348 |
| Effective tax rate | 14.1% | 20.8% | — |
| Operating cash flow (US$m) | 2,151 | 1,390 | — |
| Net debt (US$m) | 12,900 | 13,300 | — |
| Total debt outstanding (US$m) | ~14,000 | — | — |

*Source: Form 10-K body extract (`101a0b13d6c5f568.txt`), MD&A and non-GAAP reconciliation tables.*

**Revenue:** The 10-K About section cites “$23 billion in annual sales.” The consolidated income statement line items are not present in the downloadable body extract. **Fallback to Yahoo (`financials_annual.json`):** total revenue US$23.51 billion (FY2026), US$15.01 billion (FY2025), US$13.64 billion (FY2024). The FY2025–FY2026 step-up reflects full-year Berry consolidation. Flexible packaging accounted for ~55% of consolidated net sales in FY2026 (10-K).

**Profitability trend:** GAAP net income troughed in FY2025 (US$511 million) amid merger accounting (US$133 million inventory step-up amortisation, US$169 million transaction costs, US$97 million restructuring). FY2026 shows recovery driven by higher earnings base and lower effective tax rate (14.1% vs 20.8%), partly from return-to-provision adjustments. Adjusted metrics provide a cleaner through-cycle view: adjusted EBIT rose 63% year-on-year to US$2.8 billion, indicating underlying operating improvement beyond one-offs.

**Cash flow:** Operating cash flow increased US$761 million year-on-year to US$2.15 billion, “primarily driven by higher net income, adjusted for non-cash items, partially offset by higher working capital outflows” (10-K). Investing cash outflows fell sharply as Berry acquisition cash closed in the prior year; proceeds from FY2026 portfolio divestitures were applied to debt reduction. **Free cash flow of US$1.23 billion (FY2026) and capital expenditure of US$922 million are cited from Yahoo fallback** — the 10-K confirms OCF but does not surface capex in the extracted sections reviewed.

**Balance sheet and leverage:** Net debt declined modestly to US$12.9 billion (from US$13.3 billion). Total debt was US$14.0 billion at 30 June 2026, including US$1.29 billion drawn on a US$3.75 billion revolving facility. Interest expense rose 71% to US$676 million, “primarily driven by the additional debt issued and assumed in the Merger” (10-K). Approximately 15% of indebtedness is variable-rate. Tangible book value is deeply negative (goodwill and intangibles of ~US$18.7 billion per Yahoo fallback), a structural feature of serial packaging M&A.

**Covenants:** Bank facilities require leverage not higher than 3.9x (stepping to 4.25x for twelve months post-acquisitions above US$375 million). As of 30 June 2026, Amcor was **in compliance with all applicable covenants** (10-K). No going-concern qualification is present.

**Interim / quarterly:** **No Amcor plc interim filing bodies (Form 10-Q or ASX half-year) are available in `filings_index.json`.** The three indexed “interim” entries belong to Amur Minerals and must be disregarded. For directional context only (Yahoo fallback, not primary): Q4 FY26 (period ended 30 June 2026) revenue US$6.40 billion and net income US$389 million; Q3 FY26 revenue US$5.91 billion, net income US$278 million. Quarterly earnings improved through the second half, consistent with integration progress reported in news coverage, but this cannot be verified against filing bodies.

**Integration costs:** The Berry Plan carries an estimated pre-tax cash cost of ~US$280 million (restructuring and integration), with US$107 million net cash outflows to date (10-K). Restructuring and related expenses were US$215 million in FY2026 versus US$64 million in FY2025.
risks_and_flags:
**Leverage and interest-rate exposure.** The 10-K explicitly warns that “significant indebtedness may limit flexibility and increase borrowing costs,” with ~15% of debt on variable rates. Interest expense of US$676 million consumes a material share of EBIT. Management has executed debt refinancings and early redemptions (e.g., US$1.5 billion notes redeemed January 2026; US$1.5 billion new notes issued March 2026), but deleveraging remains a multi-year requirement. Credit-rating maintenance may constrain buybacks or dividend growth if integration disappoints.

**Merger and integration execution.** Berry integration is the dominant near-term risk. Restructuring charges, inventory step-up, and executive transition costs (US$15 million in FY2026) have distorted GAAP comparability. Failure to deliver synergies — the 10-K states full synergies are expected to “further increase cash generation” but does not quantify the run-rate in the extracted sections — would leave Amcor carrying Berry-level debt without Berry-level returns.

**Goodwill and intangible asset risk.** The 10-K flags “a significant write-down of goodwill and/or other intangible assets” as a forward-looking risk. Post-merger intangibles amortisation was US$558 million in FY2026 (up from US$246 million in FY2025), mechanically suppressing GAAP earnings. A impairment would be non-cash but would signal overpayment for Berry.

**Customer concentration and cyclicality.** Risk factors cite loss of key customers, customer consolidation, and changes in consumer demand patterns across FMCG end markets. Packaging demand is defensive relative to mining or discretionary retail, but volume softness in consumer goods (referenced in news coverage, July–August 2026) can pressure organic growth.

**Regulatory and sustainability.** Extended producer responsibility, plastic regulation, and customer sustainability mandates require ongoing R&D (US$170 million in FY2026). Failure to meet recyclability/recycled-content targets could erode share with large FMCG customers.

**Pension and employee benefits.** Defined benefit plan obligations are referenced in Note 13; FY2026 “Other” adjustments include pension settlements (10-K). Employee benefit liabilities of US$309 million are on the balance sheet (Yahoo fallback).

**Governance / data quality.** The filings index contamination with Amur Minerals RNS announcements is a material research-process red flag for this ticker. Investors relying on automated filing ingestion should verify all primary documents via ASX/NYSE/SEC directly.

**Dividend sustainability.** News coverage (AFR, 13 April 2026: “The quarterly dividend habit Amcor can’t afford to kick”) and Morningstar (4 June 2026: “Will Amcor lose its dividend aristocrat status?”) highlight market concern that the elevated payout ratio post-merger may constrain balance-sheet repair. FY2026 cash dividends paid were US$1.20 billion against free cash flow of US$1.23 billion (Yahoo fallback) — tight coverage.

news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is **moderate in substance but voluminous in price-commentary** — Kalkine and similar outlets dominate; substantive corporate news clusters around the Berry integration and FY2026 results.

**M&A / strategy**
- Berry Global merger completed April 2025; integration and synergy capture remain the dominant strategic theme (“Amcor (ASX:AMC) Strengthens Global Packaging Platform After Berry Global Integration,” Kalkine, 27 August 2026; “Why Is Amcor (ASX:AMC) in Focus as It Details packaging integration progress?,” Kalkine, 1 September 2026).
- Portfolio rationalisation: non-core divestitures and strategic review noted in 10-K; news references integration-driven platform expansion.

**Earnings**
- FY2026 Q4 results (August 2026): “Amcor Q4 adjusted profit soars 40% on Berry integration” (Yahoo Finance, 13 August 2026); earnings call cited 32% EBITDA growth and ~US$285 million synergies (Yahoo Finance transcript summary, 13 August 2026). “Amcor earnings: Net sales rocket 68% on Berry deal; guidance reaffirmed” (Motley Fool Australia, 4 February 2026 — H1 context).

**Capital actions**
- One-for-five reverse stock split completed January 2026 (“Amcor Completes One-for-Five Reverse Stock Split,” Mirage News, 16 January 2026).
- Dividend increased post-split; ex-dividend coverage in September 2026 (“Dividend Stock on Watch: Amcor plc (ASX:AMC) Trades Ex-Dividend Thursday,” Kalkine, 2 September 2026). ASX notice: US$0.65 quarterly dividend (12 August 2026).

**Management**
- Former Amcor flexibles leader departing to Kaiser Aluminum CEO role (Yahoo Finance, 18 August 2026) — minor talent-flow signal, not a top-level Amcor CEO change.

**Analyst / income-investor debate**
- Motley Fool Australia (11 August 2026): “Amcor shares have surged 30% since May. Buy, hold or sell?”
- Dividend yield articles recurring May–July 2026 (Motley Fool, fool.com.au) citing 5.5–7% yield range.
- AFR (13 April 2026): dividend sustainability scrutiny.

**Operational / ESG**
- Product wins: 30% PCR film supply to Tiptree (Yahoo Finance, 25 August 2026); Ocean Potion sunscreen packaging partnership (14 August 2026).

**Thin areas:** Limited sell-side initiation/downgrade coverage in the manifest; most items are syndicated commentary rather than primary investigative reporting. No material regulatory enforcement actions surfaced.
research_rationale: Filing-backed FY2026 earnings and cash-flow inflection post-Berry merger support the quantitative buy signal on business quality grounds, but unpopulated screen metrics, heavy leverage, tight dividend/FCF coverage, and absent interim filing bodies prevent full confirmation of the value case.
